_source: THE VT RULE BOOK OF RECORD (Spec Kit 071). Finalised from specs/071-vehicle-tracking-analytics/rules-draft.json; the evidence for every value is in that draft, spec.md (F1-F12, A1-A12, D7) and specs/vt-analytics/workbook-rules.md. The operative copy is VT_RULES inlined in nicks_code/vt-engine.js (the apps run from file://): every key here that does not start with '_' must equal VT_RULES field by field - nicks_code/diagnostics/verify-vt-rules.mjs fails on drift. Change both together, with a dated _changes[] entry.

_changes.why: first rule book of record; _evidence prose dropped (it lives in the draft and the spec), _cells kept

the draft said 'must equal MTD_RULES.vat', and MTD_RULES.vat is the MULTIPLIER 1.15 (specs/mtd_engine_rules.json reference_data.vat_multiplier); stored the same way so the equality is literal. Fitted value = charge ex VAT x vat

the one-off 4 Nov 2026 election holiday (MTD_RULES.extraHolidays, mirrored; verify-vt-rules fails if the two differ). It explains A4: the November cycle has 23 weekdays and the Sales Review budgets 22 dialing days
the chain keys are the seller_match values stored on the case (plan DB-2)
US2-2: an agent with no in-play case this business month is listed as notRated why 'nodata', never shown a zero score

A6 made operative: a case first seen on the book's opening extract (book.openedOn) has no sale day unless the opening book supplies one; working days for the rating start the day after the opening extract when no opening book was loaded

_changes.by: Spec Kit 071 derived-cancellation builder (owner: "ok do the recommend fix")
_changes.why: No upload carries a cancellation (BI Active Fitted is active-only: Contract Status Active on all 19,404 rows, Contract Deactivate Date blank on every row; S&M Status holds attempts only), but the hand report marks 90 of the 93 current-month sales that are in NEITHER 10 Nov file Cancelled (97 %). A Scheduled/Missed case absent from both files of a complete extract day is now Cancelled, reason dropped; a BI row with a deactivate date or a non-Active Contract Status is Cancelled, reason deactivated. Cancelled is a count (0 when none) and Cancellation % = cancelled / sales sits beside the 5 % budget. Supersedes spec A8 ('Cancelled not invented').

the exact trigger: evaluated by the commit of an extract day's second file, against that day's two files, only when no later extract day is complete; a dropped case returns on a file of its cancellation day or later; a deactivated case only on a newer Active BI row; a fitted case is never cancelled by absence
an explicit deactivation in the BI file wins over Fitted for that case (R4)
the two BI contract columns, read by position (else by name), optional: a file without them deactivates nothing

_changes.to: Cancelled count; canRate = cancelled / sales; canBudget = budgets[cycle].cancelled[sub]; fitDone keeps an install that was later deactivated
_changes.why: R6; denominators stay ALL the set's sales (a cancelled sale stays in Sales, as the hand report's Sale Count = 1 on cancelled rows)

_changes.by: the owner, choosing 'Two drivers (Recommended)' after an executive review of the score (Barry: 'you can't have missed and fitted - it's double counting ... a double minus on your score'); built by the Spec Kit 071 two-driver builder
_changes.from: vt-1.1: four drivers targetAch 35 / fitRate 30 / missRate 20 (lower) / fitted 15
_changes.to: vt-1.2: two drivers targetAch 50 / fitRate 50; Missed Rate and Fitted vs target shown, never scored
_changes.why: DOUBLE COUNTING. Once a sale is scheduled it ends fitted or not; Missed Rate scored the same unfitted sale Fitment Rate already scores, and Fitted vs target (target x days x fitment budget) re-scored Target Achievement x Fitment Rate. For an agent with 60 sales, 3 missed (5 %) scored 20/20 on Missed Rate, 4 missed (6.7 %) 10/20, 6 missed (10 %) 0/20, and the same missed sale also lowered Fitment Rate and Fitted vs target: about 12 points for ONE sale. Now every outcome counts once: a missed or cancelled sale lowers Fitment Rate only. Measures, targets, scored-when rules, the half-of-target floor, renormalisation and the VAS bands are unchanged; the lower-is-better code path stays in the engine (tested) for future use. Landed before the first VT figures were published, so no agent's published score changes. The worked example (fictional CB9101) moves from 59.7 Needs support to 61.7 Building

_changes.by: the owner ("this bi is not the same for vas its two different"), built by the incident hotfix
_changes.why: detection.vtBiFitted matches by header but the header is shared with the VAS BI Active export; the slot and the file name ('Fitted') decide (incident 2026-11-24: the VAS 'BI Active 231126.xlsx', 31,712 rows, was taken by the Vehicle Tracking intake, so VAS got no BI and the real Fitted file was then refused as thin against its 1,982 cases). A BI-columned file is Vehicle Tracking only when dropped on the VT BI slot, or its name matches nameHint (case-insensitive), or it is dropped with no slot inside the Vehicle Tracking app; otherwise it is the VAS BI Active export, exactly as before spec 071. A nameHint file on the VAS BI slot is refused. Ops and the Rake read the same hint; Scheduled & Missed and the opening book stay Vehicle Tracking by their columns alone.

spec 072, the consolidated VT Report dashboard. Adds the workbook's four views, its campaign-to-channel map, its per-channel cycle budgets, its straight-line forecast rule, a fifth lead-time bucket, the Schedulers Data column map and the three integrity checks. NOTHING in rating.* changes: owner decision D2, settled 2026-11-24 after an executive review of the score, and verify-vt-rating.mjs passes byte-for-byte.

_changes.to: read by position, Schedulers Data row 1
_changes.why: spec 072 A2. The Schedulers Data header row read verbatim: Month, Date, Agent, Sale Count, GWP, Case Number, Customer Contact, Campaign/Partner, Referring Agent, Scheduler, Result, Hrs Ahead, Date Scheduled, (blank), Scheduled, Missed, Fitted, Channel. Read by POSITION like every other VT source. 'Result' is parsed but NEVER applied (status precedence is unchanged, spec FR-012); 'Customer Contact' (col G) is customer data and is discarded in the browser before anything is sent.
spec F0-22: Schedulers Data col G is named explicitly so no later reader has to infer that it is a customer field.

_changes.by: Spec Kit 072 Phase A builder (owner decision D1)
_changes.to: the Schedulers Data sheet as a full, re-uploadable upload
_changes.why: D1: the Schedulers Data sheet becomes an upload with its own slot, superseding 'Opening book (once)'. It is the SAME sheet, now read for the three facts the daily exports do not carry — Scheduler (col J), GWP (col E) and the true sale Date (col B) — which is what unlocks the scheduler pivots, real Fitted GWP and exact daily and weekly sales. detection.vtOpeningBook is left in place for this phase: Phase B (tasks B1 and B5) replaces parseOpeningBook with parseSchedulers and retires the old slot, and the DB kind 'opening_book' stays legal so historical receipts still read (plan U-3).

Exco Summary B26:C32 is the campaign-to-channel mapping and Schedulers Data col R is =IF(H blank, blank, IFERROR(INDEX(channels, MATCH(H, campaigns, 0)), 'Other')) — exact match, unmapped falls to Other. All seven campaigns in the owner's file are mapped and Other holds exactly one record (spec F0-16). The Sales Review labels Lead Gen as 'Digital' and groups Referral + Predictive as 'Panimax', which is a roll-up and never a raw channel. This is the LEAD-SOURCE dimension, not the agent's sub-campaign (spec FR-027).

Exco Summary C4 with helper cells Z2 and Z4:AB5, and Agent & Scheduler Summary C4 with AL2 and AL4:AN5: CHOOSE over MATCH of the four labels. The cycle view restricts pre-cycle records to Result = Fitted (AB5 = IF(Z2=1,'Fitted','*')). openOutcomesInCycleOnly records the asymmetry found in the cells (spec F0-9): Sales Review C88-C92 (scheduled), C70-C74 (missed) and C76-C80 (cancelled) carry NO pre-cycle term, while sales C52-C56 and fitments C58-C62 do. K17 reads OK precisely because of it, and adding a pre-cycle term to the open outcomes would break the reconciliation.

_changes.by: Spec Kit 072 Phase A builder (owner decision D5/D6)
_changes.why: Schedulers Data col L is a five-way nested IF: 24 / 48 / 72 / '72+ in cycle' / '72+ out cycle'. The engine had four, which no page could reconcile against Sales Review K18 (C93+C99+C105+C111+C117 = C87). The split is DISPLAY ONLY: rating.notScored.hrsAhead already excludes the buckets from the score, so the two drivers (Target Achievement 50, Fitment Rate 50), their weights, the half-of-target floor, the bands and every budgets[cycle].fitment value are untouched and verify-vt-rating.mjs passes byte-for-byte (spec FR-033, D6). The only figures that move anywhere in the suite are the '72+' column on the MTD 'Hrs Ahead' table and the matching table in agent/vt-view.js, each becoming two columns. The in-cycle cutoff is the cycle end from periods.cycleByKey, NOT the workbook's DATE(YEAR(TODAY()),MONTH(TODAY())+(DAY(TODAY())>25),25) expression (spec FR-032), and the bucket stays computed from the FROZEN as-at date (hrsAsAt = latest extract + hrsAheadAsAtOffsetDays), never TODAY(): on the owner's own file the two are the same day (spec F0-14).

the workbook's own week window is date >= week start AND date < week start + 7 (Exco Summary C67 et seq.), which is what periods.weeksOf already produces; it is written down so the Performance Trend panel can cite it (spec FR-022). hrsAheadBasis states decision D5 in the rule book rather than only in the spec.

_changes.by: Spec Kit 072 Phase A builder (owner decision D2)
_changes.to: per cycle key, per channel, from the Sales Review cells
_changes.why: D2: the workbook's targets are authoritative for this dashboard. Every value is a Sales Review cell, in the rule book and never in page code, and each is carried in an operative cells{} so the page can name it on screen. Deliberately a SEPARATE branch from budgets[cycle]: budgets is per SUB-CAMPAIGN per tenure for the RATING (digital/predictive/referral/scheduling, from Sales_Review_YTD 2026.xlsx), cycleBudget is per CHANNEL for the DASHBOARD (lead_gen/referral/predictive, from this workbook). They are different dimensions over different workbooks and merging them is the most likely way to break the rating (plan risk 1). Each screen names which it measures against (D3).

_changes.by: Spec Kit 072 Phase A builder (owner decision D3)
_changes.why: Sales Review B94 = 0.75*B88, B100 = 0.1*B88, B106 = 0.05*B88, B112 = 0.05*B88, B118 = 0.05*B88 — the 10 % scheduled target apportioned 75/10/5/5/5. budgets[cycle].hrsShare (80/10/5/5) is LEFT EXACTLY AS IT IS: it comes from a different workbook ('VT Digital'!N...) and belongs to the MTD table. Both are real, both stay, and each screen labels which one it is measuring against (spec FR-034). Neither is scored.

Sales Review F51 = IFERROR(C51/$C$49*$B$49,''), where B49 = NETWORKDAYS($K$5,$K$6,$K$9:$K$14) total dialing days and C49 = NETWORKDAYS($K$5,$K$7,$K$9:$K$14) elapsed, with K7 = MIN(cycle end, MAX(sale date)) the data-through date. The holiday range K9:K14 holds 2026-11-04 and nothing else, which is ALREADY periods.extraHolidays here and MTD_RULES.extraHolidays in VAS — confirmed in both, nothing added (spec F0-7). The engine's existing periods.workingDaysBetween is the one implementation, and the label is mandatory because the figure is a pace, not a prediction (spec FR-040).

_changes.by: Spec Kit 072 Phase A builder (owner decision D4)
_changes.why: D4: the mockup's 'Budget vs Spend' card is sales against the 3,030 cycle sales budget with the straight-line forecast beside it. There is NO spend or cost figure in any of the eight sheets, in either daily export, or on the Agent List, and none may ever be invented or implied.

Sales Review K17 = IF(SUM(B43:E43)=F43,'OK','CHECK') and K18 = IF(C93+C99+C105+C111+C117=C87,'OK','CHECK'), plus a third the guide never mentions: Agent & Scheduler Summary E36 = IF(C39=$B$7,'Reconciles to total sales in view','Check: N sales in view have no scheduler name') (spec F0-23). All three read OK on the owner's real data: 1996+373+128+208 = 2705, and 130+68+26+0+149 = 373. They are engine VERDICTS, shown with an icon and the words, never colour alone, and a failing check never blocks the page (spec FR-050 to FR-054).

Exco Summary B11-B14 are the workbook's own headline sentences, built by formula from the figures above them. They are reproduced as templates filled from the model so no insight on the page is ever hand-written, and each names the number and the cell it came from (spec FR-042, FR-043). A template whose data is absent is omitted, never padded.

_changes.from: schedulerPivots built false, why 'no upload names the scheduler'
_changes.to: built true, plus the four other report shapes
_changes.why: the reason it was false is gone: D1's Schedulers Data upload names the scheduler (col J). The four pivot sheets divide each outcome by that scheduler's own grand total via GETPIVOTDATA and are ALL DATA, every page field '(All)' — grand total 3,010, matching the full record count. The workbook's percentages are not consistently divide-by-zero guarded; ours are (spec FR-045). Six schedulers in the file, exactly the headcount budget of 6, with fitted rates from 62.3 % to 84.9 % — the widest actionable spread in the workbook (spec F0-17). Schedulers resolve to a CB through the existing chain against the Agent List's 'scheduling' sub-campaign, which teams.keys and teams.notRated already carry (spec F0-18).

plan U-4: on a Schedulers Data commit every case in the sheet takes col B as its sale date, and sold_basis records which source won so 'why did this case move months?' is a query and not an archaeology. A Schedulers Data commit sets book.openingBookOn with the opening book's EXACT semantics, so model()'s trackFrom, the working-day count and therefore every published SPD and target-achievement figure do not move (plan U-5, risk 2). The merge branch itself is Phase B task B2.

vtSchedulers._phase: spec 072 task B1 switches detect() and the parser over to this key and retires vtOpeningBook; Phase A only records it. No VAS export carries a sheet named 'Schedulers Data', so unlike the BI file this detection needs no name hint and no slot tiebreak — its columns alone decide. 'result' is required as a header so a half-built sheet is refused, but its VALUE is never applied.

schedulers._discardWhy: A = Month label ('Current'/'Rollover'), not a date field. G = Customer Contact, CUSTOMER DATA, discarded. L = Hrs Ahead, a TODAY()-dependent formula we recompute frozen from periods.leadTimeBuckets. N = blank by design. O/P/Q = reference helpers, not outcome fields. R = the Channel formula, which we recompute from channels.campaignMap.

_quirks.referringAgentZero: col I is the NUMBER 0, not blank, when there is no referrer — 2,382 of 3,010 rows. A blank test reports every sale as a referral (spec F0-19).
_quirks.apptSerialZero: a blank col M reads as serial 0 (renders 1899-12-29), not empty (spec F0-20).
_quirks.emptyRows: 16,950 of the 19,960 rows in the sheet's range are EMPTY — they carry only the extended L and R formulas. The guide's '19,960 data rows' is wrong; the populated count is 3,010 (spec F0-1). Count rows, never trust the range.
_quirks.saleCountAlwaysOne: col D = 1 on every populated row and all 3,010 case numbers are distinct (spec F0-3). A file with a repeated case number is REFUSED whole, naming the duplicates, in the pattern of publish_agent_list's duplicate-CB refusal.
